children: Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc.

TMO recently unveiled the Thermo Scientific EMPAD G2 detector to help researchers analyze materials in unprecedented detail. This development is expected to bolster the company’s Analytical Instruments segment.
TMO Stock Outlook Following the News
After the announcement, TMO shares dipped slightly by 0.8% last Thursday.

On a positive note, Thermo Fisher has steadily ramped up R&D investments in recent years, fueling new product launches and enhancing its portfolio. We expect the latest development to improve investor sentiment toward TMO stock and support its upward momentum in the near term.

Thermo Fisher has a market capitalization of $233.20 billion. The company’s earnings yield of 4% is well ahead of the industry’s -1.3% yield. It surpassed earnings estimates in each of the trailing four quarters, delivering an average surprise of 4.4%.
About TMO’s EMPAD G2 Detector

EMPAD G2 enables high-speed four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D STEM), an advanced form of electron microscopy. It aims to help researchers capture more information about materials in a single scan, recording both the strongest and weakest signals without sacrificing imaging speed or data quality.

The advanced 4D STEM technology offers faster, more reliable and user-friendly performance, helping researchers accelerate discoveries in semiconductors, energy and advanced materials while supporting the development of technologies with real-world applications.
Performance and Workflow of TMO’s EMPAD G2

EMPAD G2 runs at 10,000 frames per second (0.1 ms/frame), with exceptionally high single-frame dynamic range (>10???), single-electron sensitivity and operation across the full 30–300 kV range. EMPAD G2 supports advanced applications, ranging from strain mapping and differential phase contrast (DPC) to multi-slice electron ptychography for three-dimensional characterization at the atomic scale.

EMPAD G2 is also fully integrated with the user-friendly Thermo Scientific Velox software. Researchers can collect and analyze multiple types of data, including simultaneous 4D STEM and energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (EDS) within a single workflow. This integration helps simplify advanced materials analysis and supports more reliable, repeatable results.
Industry Prospects Favor TMO
Per a QYResearch report, the global 4D STEM market was valued at an estimated $68 million in 2024 and is projected to reach $110 million by 2031, reflecting a CAGR of 6.6% from 2025 to 2031.

As 4D STEM becomes more widely adopted in academic and industrial research, detector performance is becoming increasingly important. Researchers need to capture large volumes of information rapidly while accurately measuring signals ranging from extremely strong to extremely weak. EMPAD G2 is specifically designed to meet these demands, enabling researchers to obtain reliable quantitative information from a single acquisition.
TMO: Another Key Development

Thermo Fisher recently launched Thermo Scientific Orbitrap Isora Mass Spectrometer and Orbitrap Isora Pro Mass Spectrometer, the company’s first Orbitrap instruments with a dedicated isotope ratio analysis mode. Combined with the Thermo Scientific Vanquish Duo UHPLC System and new Isotope Discoverer Software, the instruments form an integrated workflow designed to make molecular-level isotope ratio analysis accessible to more laboratories and researchers worldwide.
